title: Navigate from IntelliJ stack frames to dumped L2 classes and .l2 files
description:
When debugging a live VM in IntelliJ, stack frames in generated JVMChunk
classes cannot be navigated: neither to the dumped .class file nor, ideally,
to the .l2 text, whose line numbers the class's LineNumberTable already
records.  Making this work would let a JVM debugger step through L2 code.

What exists (optimizer/jvm/JVMTranslator.kt, with debugJVM enabled):
- Each chunk's .class is dumped under debug/jvm/<package path>/ (relative
  to the process working directory, so avail/debug/jvm when run from
  avail/), beside its .l1, .l2, .dot, and .simple.dot files.
- The class records SourceFile as the .l2 file name, e.g. "0000
  group_by_#1.l2", and its line numbers refer to lines of that .l2 file.
- Class names are derived from module and method names, e.g.
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.Maps.0000_group_by_#1 (2).group_by_#1.
  The package segments contain spaces, parentheses, '#', and characters
  such as '«', which are not Java identifiers.

Likely causes to investigate:
- The debugger resolves a frame's source as <package dirs>/<SourceFile>
  under a source root; debug/jvm is not a source root, and the .l2 file
  is not where that lookup would place it, or IntelliJ cannot map the
  non-identifier package names to directories at all.
- The class files are not on any classpath IntelliJ knows about.

Possible directions: sanitize generated package and class names to valid
identifiers (keeping a readable mapping), lay out the dump so that
<package dirs>/<SourceFile> names the .l2 file exactly, and register
debug/jvm as a source root (or document how to attach it) so the .l2 file
opens at the frame's line.
notes:
Findings (2026-11-06, verified by Mark in IntelliJ):
- Generated classes now use Java-identifier names:
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<Module>.L<line>_<function>_v<n>.<function>,
  dumped under avail/debug/jvm mirroring the package
  (JVMTranslator.prepareOutputDirectory).
- IntelliJ's Java debugger finds a frame's source by looking up a Java file
  that declares the class, through its index, within the run configuration's
  module scope.  A plain .l2 file declares nothing, so it is never found.
  Hence JVMTranslator.dumpL2ListingAsJava = true: the listing is written as
  <function>.java, declaring the class, with the listing in a comment on
  unchanged lines.
- avail/.idea/misc.xml had the project compiler output set to
  $PROJECT_DIR$/debug/jvm, and IntelliJ never indexes the project output
  directory.  Changed to $PROJECT_DIR$/out (misc.xml is untracked).
- IntelliJ setup that works: avail/debug/jvm as a content root of module
  avail.main, marked Sources, and listed under Settings > Compiler >
  Excludes (the project builds with IntelliJ's own compiler,
  delegatedBuild = false, so the stubs must not be compiled).  A Gradle
  re-sync may drop the content root.
- Register names (r0, i1, ...) come from the class's LocalVariableTable,
  now emitted whenever debugJVM is on; locals are not initialized, so a
  register not yet written shows no meaningful value.
Remaining option if the .java form is unwanted: an IntelliJ plugin with a
PositionManagerFactory mapping avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.* frames to
debug/jvm/<sourcePath>, which would make plain .l2 work.
Preferred solution (Mark, 2026-11-06): Kotlin listings with the original
class names.  JVMTranslator.l2ListingFormat = L2ListingFormat.KOTLIN and
useOriginalClassNames = true.  Each generated class lives in package
avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<module>.<line>_<function> (<n>) and its
listing is <function>.kt, declaring the class with every name segment in
backticks and the listing inside a block comment (both /* and */ broken
apart, since Kotlin comments nest).  Verified in IntelliJ: double-clicking
a generated frame opens the .kt listing at the right L2 instruction, and
register locals (r0, i1, ...) show by name.  kotlinc 2.4.21 compiles these
listings to classes with exactly the generated names; '%' only draws a
Windows warning.

The JAVA format (with Java-identifier names, useOriginalClassNames = false)
and the plain TEXT format (.l2, not navigable) remain selectable.

IntelliJ setup that navigation needs: debug/jvm is a content root of module
avail.main marked Sources, listed under Compiler > Excludes, and the project
output (misc.xml) is NOT debug/jvm (it was, which stopped indexing).

title: Autocompletion in the Avail module editor
description:
Offer completions while typing in an Avail module editor (anvil/AvailEditor.kt,
anvil/text/CodePane.kt).  Use the parsing state at the caret, via
ParsingPlanInProgressDescriptor (descriptor/parsing/), to determine what can
come next: the tokens that would advance an in-progress message plan, and the
in-scope variables whose types fit an argument position the plan expects.

No completion support exists in anvil/ yet.

title: Complete the Avail debugger
description:
Finish the Anvil debugger (avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/anvil/debugger/
AvailDebugger.kt).

Unwired actions: stepOutAction ("Out", shift-F8), stepToLineAction
("To Line"), and restartAction ("Restart") are disabled and only show a
"not implemented" dialog.

Layout: the debugger's panes have no resize bars.  AvailWorkbench uses
JSplitPane for this; the debugger should do the same.

Smaller gaps: two TODOs in AvailDebugger.kt about preserving the variable
selection when the selected frame changes.

title: L2 function inlining
description:
Inline called functions into the caller's L2 control flow graph.

Context for breaking it down: Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 9.2 notes
that L2ValueManifest.transform (currently without callers) is intended for
inlining called graphs, where the callee's stack slots must be distinguished
from the caller's via Frame, and that post-phi data keyed by semantic values
must be transformed along with it.  Survey what inlining the optimizer already
does before proposing children.

title: Remove what post-phi data makes unnecessary; add the never-used exclusion pass
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 8 lists mechanisms the post-phi data makes
unnecessary, and a never-used exclusion pass it makes possible.  Remove the
former and add the latter, once the invariants of the sibling beads are
asserted.

title: Postpone, rather than drop, inputs read only by postponed instructions
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5 (closing note) and 10.4: an input that
is read only by a postponed instruction must itself be postponed rather than
dropped.  Check whether this holds today; fix it if not.  The failure it
causes resembles the ones the post-phi design exists to end.

title: Assert each output edge is at least as informative as its input edge
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md sections 6 and 10.3: after regeneration and
post-phi replay, each output edge's manifest must be at least as informative
as the corresponding input edge's (the monotonicity law).  Add a per-edge
assertion.  Verify against testSemanticRestrictionOfSetCreation_1.

title: Assert the witness invariant on each post-phi capture
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5: every synonym captured in post-phi
data must have a witness, namely a register holding it, a constant
restriction, or a self-describing member.  Assert this at capture time.  It is
the property the design turns on, and it would catch a value whose only
witness was a postponement.

title: Finish the declared-manifest-effects design
description:
The post-phi data mechanism (L2BasicBlock.postPhiData) is captured, replayed,
and rendered, but the remaining items of the design in
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Declared_Manifest_Effects.md (its "Suggested
order", items 2, 3, 4, and 5) were not found in the code.  Read that doc
(sections 4-8) first.

title: Bring Variable_elision.md in line with the implementation
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Variable_elision.md says "This is not exactly
what was implemented", and its "Reworked form (proposed ~Oct 12, 2024)" section
describes L2_VIRTUAL_GET_VARIABLE / L2_VIRTUAL_SET_VARIABLE, which do not exist.
Rewrite it to describe the variable elision the optimizer actually performs.
The reworked design, if still wanted, is tracked by its own bead.

title: Delete Configuration_Cache_Fixes_Needed.md
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Configuration_Cache_Fixes_Needed.md lists Gradle
configuration-cache fixes for avail/build.gradle.kts.  They have landed: the

description:
FocusFilter and NoFilter (L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizationFilter.kt) are
implemented and wired into L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizer.  Turn
avail/doc/Optimization/Focus_Filter_Design_Summary.md into a description of the
filter as built (or fold it into the KDoc of
L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizationFilter, whichever reads better), and delete

title: Fold manifest invariants into L2ValueManifest KDoc; retire the session notes
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/TODO_Documentation_Updates.md and
avail/doc/Optimization/Debugging_Session_2025-01-26.md are session notes, not
design.  Move their lasting content into KDoc on L2ValueManifest (and its
neighbors) where it is still true of the current code:
- populated versus postponed semantic values, and the invariant tying a value
  with no definitions to its postponed instruction;
- hasSemanticValue versus hasLiveSemanticValue, equivalentSemanticValue
  versus equivalentPopulatedSemanticValue;
- SSA uniqueness applies to registers, not semantic values (merge points
  create several registers for one value).
Check each claim against the code (the manifest was redesigned since 2025).
Then delete both note files (ask Mark before deleting).

title: Rewrite Declared_Manifest_Effects.md as a normative design doc
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Declared_Manifest_Effects.md carries a status
line ("proposed, started"), dates, and a "Suggested order" section.  Rewrite it
to describe post-phi data as it exists: L2BasicBlock.postPhiData, when it is
captured, when it is replayed after phi generation, why postponed instructions
are not captured (witnesses), the monotonicity law, and its rendering in
L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizer.  The unfinished items in its suggested order are
tracked by the "Finish the declared-manifest-effects design" epic.

title: Rewrite Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md as a normative design doc
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md is written as
a plan (Status line, Step 1-8 sequence, "Next" sections, progress notes).  Most
of it has landed: L2SemanticUnboxedInt/Float are gone, TypeRestriction keeps
only CAN_BE_BOTTOM and IMMUTABLE flags, ValueState and Representation exist,
derivation edges replaced checkDerivedValuesHaveTheirBases, and propagation
uses ValueState.usingClasses (L2ValueManifest.propagateForRestrictionChange).

Rewrite it to describe the manifest model as it now is: ValueClass identity,
ValueState and per-kind Representation, merging, narrowing, derivation edges,
postponement, the int-register safety invariant (now i64-based, after the
64-bit widening), and the rejected alternatives that still explain the shape.
Drop status, steps, and history.  Unlanded items are tracked by their own beads
(constants, variant consistency, e-graph equivalences).  Verify every claim
against the code before keeping it.

title: Make avail/doc/Optimization normative
description:
Bring every document under avail/doc/Optimization in line with the rule that
design docs are normative: they describe the system as it is, in the present
tense, with no plan, status line, step sequence, dates, or session log.  The
plan lives in bd.  These docs are also what wovenspec (avail-docs) will serve,
so what they say must be true of the code.

title: Hoist loop-body type tests by unrolling one iteration
description: Use the result of an earlier loop generation pass to decide whether to build a variation without an inner type test that always holds (or never holds), hoisting the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.

title: Int-register conditions at loop heads
description: Specialize loop variations that keep values in int registers across the loop.

title: Drop duplicate loop variations
description: Compare a newly generated loop variation's instructions with earlier ones, and reuse a match instead of keeping a copy.

title: Generate loop-head variations and link backward branches
description: Build a loop head and body specialized for a set of conditions, and connect each backward branch to the most specific variation that satisfies it.

title: Propagate split conditions backward to loop heads
description: Carry the L2SplitConditions requested inside a loop body back along its backward branches to the loop head, so the head can be split on them.

title: Loop splitting
description:
Extend L2 code splitting to loop heads.  A loop head is split into
variations specialized for the L2SplitConditions propagated backward to it
(see avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/optimizer/L2SplitCondition.kt), and each
backward branch that closes a loop connects to the most specific available
variation of the loop head.

When a backward branch from a generated body requests conditions that no
existing variation satisfies, generate a new variation, then compare its
instructions against the previously generated variations; if it is
equivalent to one of them, reuse that one and discard the duplicate.

Kinds of condition:
- A value must be in an int register.
- A type condition tested inside the body holds (or never holds).

For a type test inside the body, use the result of a previous loop
generation pass to decide whether to create a variation without the test.
Doing so hoists the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.

title: Revive the gradle-plugin build
description:
gradle-plugin compiles (its build script now uses compilerOptions, and
AvailJarPackager is abstract), but ./gradlew build fails in validatePlugins:
AvailJarPackager, CreateAvailArtifactJar, CreateAvailProjectFileTask,
AvailAnvilTask, and PackageAvailArtifactTask must each be annotated
@CacheableTask or @DisableCachingByDefault (with a reason).  Decide per task.

Then:
- Move its Dokka plugin from 2.1.0 to the version the other builds use
  (2.3.0).  Under 2.3.0, dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml fails resolving
  dokkaHtmlGeneratorRuntimeResolver: "Edge
  org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-html-jvm:0.9.1 -> kotlin-stdlib-common:1.8.20
  has no target nodes".  avail-artifact resolves the same Dokka fine, so the
  kotlin-dsl plugin is the likely difference.
- Upgrade com.gradle.plugin-publish from 1.3.0 to 2.x (Mark held it back).
- Consider replacing -Xjvm-default=all-compatibility with its current
  Kotlin equivalent.

Verify with: cd gradle-plugin && ./gradlew build

title: Revive the avail-server build
description:
avail-server (43 Kotlin files under avail-server/src) does not build.  Its
settings.gradle.kts now includes ../avail and ../avail-artifact (as avail-cli
does), so it configures, but compilation stops at the first error:
AvailServer.kt:44 imports avail.descriptor.fiber.A_Fiber, which now lives in
avail.descriptor.representation.  The compiler reports only that first
error; expect further API drift, since the server source was last touched
2026-04-01.

Separately, its jar task captures Gradle script and Project references, which
the configuration cache rejects (4 problems, reported when storing the
configuration cache).

Verify with: cd avail-server && ./gradlew build

title: Rework variable elision around virtual get/set instructions
description:
The "Reworked form (proposed ~Oct 12, 2024)" of
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Variable_elision.md: L1Translator emits
L2_CREATE_VARIABLE plus L2_VIRTUAL_GET_VARIABLE / L2_VIRTUAL_SET_VARIABLE for
non-literal variable access, and the postponement pass applies rewrite rules
that elide variable operations.  Confirm with Mark that this design is still
wanted before starting.

title: L2_INVOKE_WITH_OUTERS: call closed code without building the closure
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Function_call_with_outers.md: the pattern
r1 = L2_CLOSE(code, outers...); L2_INVOKE(r1, args...) is common.  Replace it
with L2_INVOKE_WITH_OUTERS(code, [outers], [args]), passing outers and
arguments together on an interpreter-held argument stack (extending
argsBuffer), callee-pops (or caller-pops, to allow combining pops), cleared on
reification.  A plain L2_INVOKE of a passed-in function pushes the outers of
that function itself.

title: Variant consistency between manifest and restrictions
description:
Step 8 of the manifest redesign (Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md): keep the
variant sets in TypeRestriction (they are read where no manifest exists:
L2_GET_OBJECT_FIELD.translateToJVM, L2_GET_OBJECT_TYPE_FIELD,
L2_EXTRACT_OBJECT_VARIANT_ID, and the dispatch lookup trees).  Make the
manifest the sole writer of variant information into restrictions, reconcile
the two at every update, and have L2ValueManifest.check() assert consistency.
No such assertion exists today.

title: Constants as a ValueState field (constantOf)
description:
Step 7 of the manifest redesign (Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md): add
constantOf on the value state and remove the L2SemanticConstant special cases
from the manifest's equivalence test (avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/optimizer/
manifest/L2ValueManifest.kt, around the "otherSemanticValue is
L2SemanticConstant" cases near line 2156).  Keep L2SemanticConstant as the
canonical member; do not delete the class.

title: Focus Filter follow-ups: tests and empty-focus warning
description:
From Focus_Filter_Design_Summary.md and Focus_Filter_Integration_Plan.md:
add tests for FocusFilter (linear flow, branch with merge, focus absent,
current block given, sibling edges, loop), and warn when the focus value
appears nowhere in the graph.  Optional: filter statistics and a visual
indicator that a filter is active.
close_reason: Mark is satisfied with FocusFilter as it stands and has no plans to extend it

title: E-graph saturation for primitive-invocation equivalences
description:
Listed as out of scope in Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md: equivalences of
L2SemanticPrimitiveInvocation driven by declared theorems with a cost model
for extraction (a+a+a to a*3 unless a+a is already computed; {a,a,a} = {a};
|{a,a,a}| = 1).  ValueClass is the e-class and ValueState the e-class data; it
needs a signature table Map<Pair<Primitive, List<ValueClass>>, ValueClass>
rehashed on union.
